policy: Editorial source review, not experimental validation. Quotes are short verbatim sentences or explicitly labelled excerpts. Our proposed method and conditional unbiasedness/variance claims require our own proof and results; citations do not validate them.

reviews.description: Introduction: simulated multi-turn VLM RL and a trainer foundation. Related work: world-model rewards, structured ground-truth evaluation, historical repetition penalty.
reviews.qualification: Section 4.1 and Appendix D.2 explicitly support the reward/evaluation clauses. Whether our implementation actually includes each baseline remains an implementation/result question, not a bibliographic fact.
reviews.quote: To address reward, we developed and implemented a composite reward mechanism that combines structured evaluation with a penalty for historical repetition.

reviews.description: Introduction: VLM RL in simulation. Related work: predicted-versus-observed frames as curiosity in the same environments.
reviews.qualification: Simulation, shared environment suite, and curiosity are supported. Predicted frames is imprecise: linguistic prediction tokens are projected to visual representations and aligned with future observation embeddings; the method does not require predicting RGB frames. Recommend linguistic predictions versus observed visual representations.
reviews.quote: We introduce GLANCE, a unified framework that transforms the agent’s linguistic predictions into a source of curiosity-driven exploration.

reviews.description: Confident navigation despite missing evidence; same-state seeking versus direct navigation branches credited by later navigation returns. Introduction uses it as a same-world comparison.
reviews.qualification: The cited design is supported. Our same-prior unbiasedness statement is a conditional mathematical claim of our paper, not an unbiasedness theorem established by this citation.
reviews.quote: By comparing each evidence-seeking branch with a counterfactual direct-navigation branch from the same state

reviews.description: Deciding when to act versus obtaining clarification under uncertain information.
reviews.qualification: The information action is asking a human clarification question; do not equate it with our camera/look action.
reviews.quote: The agent must strategically ask minimal, yet relevant, clarification questions to resolve ambiguity while navigating under partial observability.

reviews.description: Compare-before-commit navigation addresses decisions under uncertain information.
reviews.qualification: This is a training-free comparator interface, not an RL credit-assignment method. Current sentence does not claim RL.
reviews.quote: We instantiate this idea in C2Nav, a training-free framework with three coordinated faculties.

reviews.description: Navigation behavior is encouraged to remain consistent across original and counterfactual environments.
reviews.qualification: Counterfactual observations are generated as linear combinations; the reference is not evidence of physically restored hidden-world pairs or RGB equality.
reviews.quote: We describe an effective algorithm to generate counterfactual observations on the fly for VLN, as linear combinations of existing environments.
reviews.locator: Abstract; following sentence states action stability

reviews.description: Flip/Stay image–text conflicts and Counterfactual Twin-Margin supervision on static data, contrasted with interactive evidence acquisition.
reviews.qualification: Flip/Stay and CTM are supported. Static data is appropriate for the paired training examples, but the paper also reports real-world video evaluation, so it should not be read as image-only evaluation or a general claim that every datum is static.
reviews.quote: uses paired interventions to teach how answer probabilities should change when the requested evidence changes

reviews.description: Edits 3D scenes to form counterfactual QA supervision for grounding, without embodied evidence-seeking action selection.
reviews.qualification: Static refers to QA supervision/evaluation, not absence of 3D scene editing. Prefer saying their supervision does not train sequential evidence acquisition.
reviews.quote: Specifically, given a grounding failure, DEER-3D first identifies the predicate-level error (e.g., attribute or spatial relation).
reviews.locator: Abstract; following sentence describes scene edits and aligned QA

reviews.description: Perturbs textual statements in adversarial self-play and verifies them against a given image, rather than acquiring new observations.
reviews.qualification: The static-image verification distinction is supported; its self-play is still an interactive training loop, so avoid using static to mean no interaction of any kind.
reviews.quote: A Challenger generates an image-grounded true claim together with a minimally perturbed hard-negative counterpart

reviews.description: Studies static VLM reasoning dependence on image inputs.
reviews.qualification: Tests image removal and introduces original/masked/perturbed visual triplets. Does not establish our embodied causal or variance claims.
reviews.quote: DVRP introduces intrinsic supervision via visual triplets, comprising original, masked, and perturbed inputs.

reviews.description: Studies how much static multimodal reasoning depends on visual input.
reviews.qualification: The source connects longer reasoning with reduced visual attention and hallucination, rather than showing that all reasoning is harmful.
reviews.quote: Attention analysis shows that longer reasoning chains lead to reduced focus on visual inputs, which contributes to hallucination.

reviews.description: Under scene-preserving language interventions, embodied policies often act toward the original goal.
reviews.qualification: The claim is about the evaluated policies and interventions; do not universalize to all VLA policies.
reviews.quote: When instructions request a different visible object, all evaluated policies predominantly approach and pick up the incorrect original target associated with the scene.

reviews.description: Unsupervised environment design generates challenging environments for an agent.
reviews.qualification: PAIRED specifically maximizes protagonist–antagonist regret to retain solvability, rather than arbitrary worst-case difficulty.
reviews.quote: We call our technique Protagonist Antagonist Induced Regret Environment Design (PAIRED).
reviews.locator: Abstract; preceding sentences specify regret and solvability

reviews.description: Unsupervised environment design evolves curricula that challenge the current agent.
reviews.qualification: The reference supports regret-guided curriculum generation, not our hidden-pair validity checks.
reviews.quote: This work proposes harnessing the power of evolution in a principled, regret-based curriculum.

reviews.description: LLM-driven environment design generates environments for agent training.
reviews.qualification: These are executable stateful environments for language agents; do not imply that SPADE itself guarantees 3D embodied physical validity.
reviews.quote: an Environment Designer that writes complete, long-horizon training environments as executable code with an OpenAI Gym-style reset()/step() interface

reviews.description: LLM-driven environment design for embodied agents with adaptive difficulty.
reviews.qualification: The platform uses an evolving coding agent and verifier feedback; this is different from our fixed information-set construction.
reviews.quote: Generated worlds are exported as Gym-style environments for embodied agent learning.

reviews.description: Quality-diversity red-teaming searches for challenging VLA environments.
reviews.qualification: The paper explicitly uses quality-diversity optimization and policy-embedding diversity.
reviews.quote: Q-DEG uses Quality Diversity (QD) optimization to find a set of high-failure environments, while promoting diversity using policy embeddings extracted from the VLA.

reviews.description: Grouped under quality-diversity red-teaming of VLA policies.
reviews.qualification: Physical red-teaming and challenging feasible scenes are supported. The method describes risk synthesis followed by trajectory-guided gradient-free risk amplification; the reviewed source does not establish that this is quality-diversity optimization. Separate Q-DEG's quality-diversity claim from RedVLA's physical red-teaming claim.
reviews.quote: It iteratively refines the risk factor state through gradient-free optimization guided by trajectory features.

reviews.description: Perturbation benchmark creates environments that challenge an agent.
reviews.qualification: The CVPR title differs from arXiv 2510.13626; use the conference bibliography while retaining the linkage. It evaluates robustness, not paired-policy credit.
reviews.quote: Our findings challenge the assumption that high benchmark scores equate to true competency
reviews.locator: Abstract; preceding text lists perturbation dimensions

reviews.description: Studies distinguishable consequences of interventions under partial observability.
reviews.qualification: Its learned latent representations distinguish action-conditioned futures; this is not a proof of exact observable-prefix equality for our simulator pairs.
reviews.quote: a contrastive counterfactual objective that separates futures induced by distinct interventions even when their observations look alike

reviews.description: General connection to classical variance reduction.
reviews.qualification: GAE uses value functions and an exponentially weighted advantage estimator, allowing bias. It does not justify our separate stratified hidden-world estimator or an unbiasedness claim; those need our own derivation.
reviews.quote: using value functions to substantially reduce the variance of policy gradient estimates at the cost of some bias

reviews.description: AI2-THOR is the interactive simulator used for our proposed construction.
reviews.qualification: The source supports navigation/object interaction; exact restoration, physical validity, and our completed implementation are not established by citing the simulator paper.
reviews.quote: AI2-THOR consists of near photo-realistic 3D indoor scenes, where AI agents can navigate in the scenes and interact with objects to perform tasks.
